picks.file: Henry Freeman James (d.1823) - View of Liverpool, c.1811 - 55.411 - Merseyside Maritime Museum.jpg
picks.what: The town and its waterfront from across the Mersey, painting (Merseyside Maritime Museum)
picks.why: only true general view of the early town; skyline with church spires and shipping; small file (1000 px)

picks.what: St. George’s Hall and Lime Street, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the city’s best-known civic scene, with the Wellington Column and trams; white border cut

picks.what: Aerial view of the city center (Britain from Above)
picks.why: St. George’s Hall, St. John’s Gardens and Lime Street Station clearly seen; trim cuts a scratch along the left edge

picks.file: A view of Liverpool from across the river - geograph.org.uk - 5478713.jpg
picks.what: Liverpool and its Anglican Cathedral from across the Mersey, photograph
picks.why: only modern skyline view among the candidates; cathedral tower dominates

notes: P3: Robert Salmon’s ‘A Packet off Liverpool’ (#3, 1809, larger file) is a ship portrait with the town hidden behind the ship; #2 is a color-inverted copy. P4: stereo views #12–13 have only a 1850–80 range. P5: 1924 aerials (#16, #17) are firmly dated and larger but show less recognizable parts of the center. P6: #21, #24, #25 are Liverpool Street station in London; #23 (Albert Dock) frames the Pier Head through columns.
